links.outcome: Classification performance of a concept-decomposable (interpretable) chest X-ray model on external datasets
links.effect: CLEAR achieved state-of-the-art classification performance on four external physician-annotated datasets while making every prediction decomposable into concept contributions; no numeric results in the abstract.
links.quote: External validation on four large, physician-annotated datasets from the United States, Europe and Asia shows that CLEAR not only achieves state-of-the-art classification performance but also enables applications: auditable zero-shot pathology detection, systematic identification of radiological confounders and the creation of expert-level concept bottleneck models from data-driven concepts.

unlisted_practices: Concept-based auditing of imaging models to systematically identify radiological confounders
Concept bottleneck models built from data-driven concepts

screen.reason: The study develops and benchmarks a new concept-based foundation model architecture (CLEAR) across retrospective datasets. While it proposes the architecture for auditability and safety, it evaluates model performance and feature attribution rather than testing an organizational deployment safeguard or guardrail practice.
